column1: # Token families that denote one operation but that the two languages spell
# differently.  Column 1 is the canonical spelling both sides compare as; column 2 is
# the comma-separated family; column 3 records why the family is legitimate.
# A family does two things: every body check canonicalises it to column 1, and the
# family gets an occurrence check (the port must use it at least as often as the C body
# does).  The occurrence check is not optional: a note that merely allowed `memcpy` to
# be absent let a body with all three of doprnt's output copies deleted pass both

column3: std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping is the port's memcpy/mempcpy; gnulib's rpl_mempcpy keeps its C name

C's `alignof` is Rust's `align_of::<T> ()`, same rule

C's memset over a byte buffer is the port's std::ptr::write_bytes (term.c's calculate_costs and tty_menu_activate); the occurrence check keeps every clear alive

the frozen target's `wchar_t` is a 16-bit unsigned integer (the Windows SDK's `WCHAR`); the port names it `c_ushort` where it declares a buffer (`[c_ushort; MAX_PATH]`), because no mirror carries `wchar_t` itself (P-88)
C's `NULL`: the port spells it per context - `None`/`.is_none ()`/`.is_some ()` for the `Option<…>` a function pointer becomes (w32.c 1160/1170), `core::ptr::null_mut ()`/`.is_null ()` for a pointer

`<winbase.h>`'s `LookupPrivilegeValue` is a `TEXT ()` macro - C's own text spells it unsuffixed and the header maps it to `…A`/`…W` by `_UNICODE`.  The port's `LPCTSTR`/`LPCSTR` are the ANSI forms (w32.c C 284's reading, the `SE_*_NAME` class), so w32.c C 7340's call is the port's in-unit `LookupPrivilegeValueA` declaration and the one token differs only by that suffix; the `unicode` arm is owed with the same three constants.
